subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos100° cos40° + sin100° sin40° = 1/2.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.87, chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 24. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark to recognising the cos(A − B) expansion and one to the standard value that closes the proof. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those slots on almost every paper. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Recognise the cos(A − B) expansion
steps.margin_note: First mark. cosA cosB + sinA sinB = cos(A − B), with A = 100° and B = 40°.
steps.memory_tip: A plus sign between the two products means a minus sign inside the bracket: cos(A − B).
lines: [∵ cosA cosB + sinA sinB = cos(A − B)]

recall.must_convey: That cosA cosB + sinA sinB = cos(A − B) is recognised, giving cos60°.
accept: cos A cos B plus sin A sin B is cos of A minus B
the left side is cos of one hundred minus forty
cos A minus B formula apply cheste cos sixty vasthundi
plus sign means minus inside the bracket

steps.why: The plus sign between the two products is the mark of cos(A − B). With a minus sign between them it would be cos(A + B) instead.
common_mistakes: Using cos(A + B), which has a minus sign between the products.

steps.label: Write the standard value
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 100° − 40° = 60° and cos60° = 1/2, which is the right hand side.

recall.must_convey: That cos60° = 1/2, which equals the right hand side.
accept: that equals the right hand side so it is proved
the difference is sixty and cos sixty is a half
cos sixty ante one by two, so proved
left hand side equals right hand side

steps.why: 60° is a standard angle, so the value is exact. Nothing has to be approximated anywhere in this proof.
common_mistakes: Stopping at cos60° without writing its value.
